title: Little Office of S. Anastasia, Martyr, Patroness and Wonderworker of the Exempt, Most Ancient, and Most Celebrated Monastery of Benediktbeuern

introductoryNotes.text: From a book of the same name published in 1702.

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen. Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. Alleluia.

blocks.source: Vel pro temporum varietate: Laus tibi Domine, Rex aeternae gloriae.
blocks.english: Or, according to the season: Praise be to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.

blocks.source: Ex stirpe nata Consulum, Amor, decusque siderum, Fausta Parentis unicum, Nostraque, salve, gaudium. Te Roma mundo protulit, Te Mater astris nutriit.
blocks.english: Born of consular stock, love and glory of the stars, fortunate one, thy parent’s unique joy and our joy, hail. Rome brought thee forth for the world; thy mother nurtured thee for the stars.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Fausta can be feminine vocative addressing Anastasia; Parentis unicum shares the printed neuter gaudium with Nostraque. Unicum agrees with gaudium, not with the parent. A grammatical adjective/apposition reading is retained without certifying a mother’s proper name or changing Fausta to Faustae. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Born of consular stock, love and glory of the stars, hail, our joy [the printed phrase Fausta Parentis unicum is uncertain]. Rome brought thee forth for the world; thy mother nurtured thee for the stars.

blocks.source: O quam pulchra est casta generatio cum claritate! Immortalis enim est memoria illius, quoniam apud Deum nota est, et apud homines.
blocks.english: O how beautiful is a chaste generation with glory! For its memory is immortal, being known with God and among men.
℣. In thy beauty and thy loveliness,

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: Concede, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus, ut beata Anastasia, quae martyrii promuit palmam, intercessionibus suis et praesentis vitae nobis remedia conferat, et aeternam salutem.Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
blocks.english: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that blessed Anastasia, [printed quae martyrii promuit palmam: unresolved verb], may through her intercessions bestow upon us remedies for this present life and eternal salvation. Through Christ our Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Promuit is not certified through the conjectural attained reading; the identical defect is visibly printed in all seven actual collects. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Et fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. And may the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: O quam te memorem, diva, Dei tui, Dum fervens teneris parvula flammulis, Et spernens generis Romulei decus, Ad altiora provolas. Succendit docilem discipulae facem Ardor Chrysogoni. Mens, radiis sacris Leges docta pias Christianismum sequi, Ridet deorum inanias.
blocks.english: O how shall I commemorate thee, holy one of thy God, while as a little girl thou burnest with tender flames, and, scorning the glory of Roman birth, fliest to higher things? The ardour of Chrysogonus kindles the receptive torch of his disciple. Thy mind, taught by sacred rays the devout laws and to follow Christianity, laughs at the vanities of the gods.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Mens/docta agree; passive doceo can retain accusative Leges pias and infinitive Christianismum sequi. Christianismum is accusative object of sequi, not a defective genitive modifying laws. Dei tui retained as genitive with diva. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O how shall I commemorate thee, holy one, while as a little girl thou burnest with tender flames for thy God, and, scorning the glory of Roman birth, fliest to higher things? The ardour of Chrysogonus kindles the receptive torch of his disciple. Thy mind, taught by sacred rays to follow the devout laws of Christianity, laughs at the vanities of the gods.

blocks.source: Domine, qui me creasti, et tulisti a me amorem saeculi, jube me ad tua misericordia pervenire.
blocks.english: Lord, Who didst create me and take from me the love of the world, command that I may [printed ad tua misericordia: unresolved governed case].
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Actual case after ad remains unresolved. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Lord, Who didst create me and take from me the love of the world, command that I may reach Thy mercy.

blocks.source: O diva, dives hortus es, Tempesque gratarum, Hic castitatis lilia, Flores benignitatis, Libertime progerminant, Fidesque pesque intentae. Sed una Christi caritas Spinae insita est merito.
blocks.english: O holy one, thou art a rich garden [the printed Tempesque gratarum is unclear]. Here lilies of chastity and flowers of kindness [printed Libertime: unresolved adverb] spring forth [the printed phrase concerning faith and hope is defective]. But the charity of Christ alone is deservedly grafted to a thorn.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Spinae is a regular dative with insita est; merito is the adverb deservedly. No need to invent among thorns. Tempesque gratarum, Libertime and Fidesque pesque remain bracketed. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O holy one, thou art a rich garden [the printed Tempesque gratarum is unclear]. Here lilies of chastity and flowers of kindness spring forth freely [the printed phrase concerning faith and hope is defective]. But the charity of Christ alone is planted among thorns [the printed concluding construction is uncertain].

blocks.source: Hortus conclusus, soror mea, hortus conclusus fons signatus. Emissiones tuae paradisus malorum Punicorum cum pomorum fructibus.
blocks.english: A garden enclosed is my sister, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed. Thy shoots are a paradise of pomegranates with the fruits of trees.
℣. Flowers have appeared in our land.

blocks.source: Viro ligata conjugii Ligata sacris artibus Astris adhaeres nexibus, Viriquae amores respuis. Hinc lora, carcer te manent, Ergastulumque foetidum: Sed altior mens libera Quiescit inter sidera.
blocks.english: Bound to a husband of marriage, bound by sacred ways, thou cleavest to the stars with bonds and rejectest [printed Viriquae: unresolved form] loves. Hence lashes, prison, and a foul workhouse await thee; but thy higher mind, free, rests among the stars.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Conjugii can qualify viro as genitive of marriage; Viriquae remains unresolved without substituting virique. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.

blocks.source: Non te deliciae, gaudia non trahunt, Non te divitiae, praemia non movent. Nec triplex Veneris machina te rapit Nec Ulpiani basia. Castis fixa Deo semper amoribus Fulges aethereo lumine gratiae. Sed perdit Cyprio cum Puero miser Sua Ulpianus lumina.
blocks.english: Pleasures do not draw thee, nor joys; riches do not move thee, nor rewards. Neither the threefold device of Venus nor Ulpian’s kisses carry thee away. Always fixed upon God in chaste loves, thou shinest with the heavenly light of grace. But miserable Ulpian loses his eyes with the Cyprian Boy.

blocks.source: Qui palma stoter largior Palmariam per Insulam, Hic Coelites Victoriam Tuum videre gestiunt. Assita lentis ignibus Moras pati jam nescia, Conquesta flammis languida, Amoris igne concidis.
blocks.english: [The printed opening Qui palma stoter largior is unintelligible.] Across the island of Palmaria, here the heavenly ones long to see [printed Victoriam Tuum: unresolved agreement/reference]. Set amid slow fires, no longer knowing how to endure delay, having complained amid the flames, languishing, thou fallest through the fire of love.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered source personally compared. Tuum does not print a feminine possessive agreeing with Victoriam; no unprinted tuam supplied. Conquesta is a regular perfect deponent participle of complain, not an unprinted conquered/overcome form. Qui palma stoter largior remains unresolved. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: [The printed opening Qui palma stoter largior is unintelligible.] Across the island of Palmaria, here the heavenly ones long to see thy victory. Set amid slow fires, no longer knowing how to endure delay, overcome and languishing in the flames, thou fallest through the fire of love.

editorialNotes.text: Prepared English was compared visually with PDF pages 432–435. The seven printed hours and commendation remain; no Lauds is added. Later opening and closing incipits expand within this office, using the non-Alleluia Prime response where printed. Later Benedicamus response signs differ from the full Matins form and remain explicitly pending. Defective hymn clauses remain provisional or unresolved.

10 October 2026: all four rendered pages and all 123 passages personally compared, including 1702 attribution, seven actual hours (no Lauds), seven fully printed collects, seasonal rubric, four Benedicamus response signs, abbreviations, hymn continuations and Commendation. Six pending passages verified: adjectival Fausta/unicum gaudium, passive-doceo/Christianismum sequi construction and four securely printed response signs. Thirteen genuine source blockers remain explicitly bracketed. Future Facesset, deponent Conquesta, dative Spinae and genitive closing Fidelium retained literally; prior English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
